items.stem: A quality-control result falls outside the laboratory's acceptable range before patient testing. The analyst should:

options.text: Withhold patient results and investigate the QC failure
options.rationale: Correct: results should not be released while QC is out of control.

options.text: Release results and note the QC issue later
options.rationale: Releasing results under failed QC risks reporting errors.

options.text: Repeat only if a clinician complains
options.rationale: QC failures must be addressed proactively.

options.text: Widen the acceptable range to pass QC
options.rationale: Altering ranges to pass QC is improper.

items.explanation: Correct: results should not be released while QC is out of control.
items.provenance: AI-drafted original item, not from any proprietary, leaked or paid exam source

items.stem: In ABO grouping, a discrepancy between forward and reverse typing most importantly requires the analyst to:

options.text: Resolve the discrepancy before reporting a blood type
options.rationale: Correct: unresolved discrepancies must not be reported.
Reporting one side of an unresolved discrepancy is unsafe.

options.text: Assume group O to be safe
options.rationale: Assuming a type without resolution is improper.
Both forward and reverse typing must agree or be resolved.

items.explanation: Correct: unresolved discrepancies must not be reported.

items.stem: Which TWO actions support accurate haematology results?

options.text: Reviewing a peripheral smear when the analyzer flags
options.rationale: Correct: smear review confirms or refutes instrument flags.

options.text: Checking the specimen for clots or haemolysis
Using an expired control to save time

items.explanation: Correct: smear review confirms or refutes instrument flags.
